input.content:
Bound the polling methods by their timeout when CDP does not answer

Tab.find, select, find_all, select_all, xpath and wait_for (and so
tab(...)), and the cloudflare helpers cf_wait_for_interactive_challenge,
cf_is_interactive_challenge_present and verify_cf only compared their
timeout between CDP round trips. While the page shows a JS dialog the
renderer never answers DOM.getDocument or DOM.enable, so these calls hung
forever instead of raising or returning at the timeout, the same problem
already fixed for wait_for_ready_state.

The polling loops now run under asyncio.wait_for. Their last attempt is
made at the deadline (the sleep between attempts is clamped to the time
left) and gets half a second to finish, so an element that shows up just
before the deadline is still found. wait_for no longer sleeps after it
found the element. Each method keeps its outcome on timeout: TimeoutError
for find, select, find_all, select_all, wait_for and verify_cf, [] for
xpath and False for cf_is_interactive_challenge_present.

With timeout <= 0, find, select, find_all, select_all and wait_for still
make their single attempt without a bound, as query_selector does, so on
a page blocked by a dialog they still hang. xpath never raises, so it
bounds its attempt even then: it gets half a second and returns [] when
no answer comes.

xpath now makes at least one attempt, so timeout <= 0 runs the query
instead of returning [] right away, and it waits half a second between
attempts instead of spinning. verify_cf runs its click phase under the
time left and clamps the click_delay sleep to the deadline, so it no
longer overruns its timeout by up to click_delay.

The bound also cuts off a slow attempt that would have succeeded. One DOM
query on a page with tens of thousands of nodes can take seconds, mostly
spent parsing the DOM.getDocument reply, so a call whose single attempt
takes longer than timeout + 0.5s now raises or returns [] where it used
to return late.

Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Bound the polling methods by their timeout when CDP does not answer

Tab.find, select, find_all, select_all, xpath and wait_for (and so
tab(...)), and the cloudflare helpers cf_wait_for_interactive_challenge,
cf_is_interactive_challenge_present and verify_cf only compared their
timeout between CDP round trips. While the page shows a JS dialog the
renderer never answers DOM.getDocument or DOM.enable, so these calls hung
forever instead of raising or returning at the timeout, the same problem
already fixed for wait_for_ready_state.

The polling loops now run under asyncio.wait_for. Their last attempt is
made at the deadline (the sleep between attempts is clamped to the time
left) and gets half a second to finish, so an element that shows up just
before the deadline is still found. wait_for no longer sleeps after it
found the element. Each method keeps its outcome on timeout: TimeoutError
for find, select, find_all, select_all, wait_for and verify_cf, [] for
xpath and False for cf_is_interactive_challenge_present.

With timeout <= 0, find, select, find_all, select_all and wait_for still
make their single attempt without a bound, as query_selector does, so on
a page blocked by a dialog they still hang. xpath never raises, so it
bounds its attempt even then: it gets half a second and returns [] when
no answer comes.

xpath now makes at least one attempt, so timeout <= 0 runs the query
instead of returning [] right away, and it waits half a second between
attempts instead of spinning. verify_cf runs its click phase under the
time left and clamps the click_delay sleep to the deadline, so it no
longer overruns its timeout by up to click_delay.

The bound also cuts off a slow attempt that would have succeeded. One DOM
query on a page with tens of thousands of nodes can take seconds, mostly
spent parsing the DOM.getDocument reply, so a call whose single attempt
takes longer than timeout + 0.5s now raises or returns [] where it used
to return late.

input.notes:
Heavy pages (reviewer item 2). I chose option (c): keep the hard bound at timeout + 0.5s and state the cost exactly. I did not add a larger or adaptive grace.

The trade-off cannot be avoided without a way to tell "Chrome is answering slowly" from "Chrome will never answer". I measured headless Chromium 141 with my own probe, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/fix/Q2/r2/probe_lag.py. It records how long the event loop is blocked during one attempt with a large timeout:

| Nodes | Call | Total | Loop blocked (Python parsing) | Loop idle (waiting for Chrome) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20k | select | 0.65s | 0.38s | 0.27s |
| 50k | select | 2.27s | 1.66s | 0.6s |
| 50k | xpath | 2.06s | 1.34s | 0.72s |
| 100k | select | 6.36s | 3.54s | 2.82s |
| 100k | xpath | 4.00s | 3.28s | 0.71s |

- Bounding only the CDP reply waits (option a) would still cut select(timeout 0.5 or 2) at 100k nodes, because Chrome alone takes about 2.8s there. It would also mean changing Connection.send.
- A "loop-lag-tolerant" timer would fix only some of the measured cases. It would also replace asyncio.wait_for with a custom timing primitive, which is risky in the last round.
- Option (b), timeout + max(0.5, timeout), would double the hang time on a blocked page (select default 10s becomes 20s) and still miss select(timeout=0.5) at 50k nodes.

Suggested changelog wording for the supervisor:
"Tab.find, select, find_all, select_all, xpath, wait_for and tab(...), and the cloudflare helpers, now return or raise within about timeout + 0.5s when the browser never answers (for example while an alert() is open), instead of hanging. With timeout <= 0, find, select, find_all, select_all and wait_for still make one attempt without a bound, so they can still hang on a page blocked by a dialog. xpath bounds its attempt to 0.5s and returns []. An attempt that takes longer than timeout + 0.5s is now cut off. On pages with tens of thousands of nodes a single DOM query can take 2-6s, so calls with short timeouts there now time out or return [] where they used to return late."

Item 4: no code change, as the reviewer said. The commit message no longer claims that these methods "no longer hang" unconditionally.

Other residual risks:
- When the bound fires, the cancelled command stays in the mapper until Chrome answers. It drained to 0 after tab.get in the alert probe.
- DOM.enable sent by xpath before a cut-off stays enabled.

Sites left alone on purpose:
- Connection._register_handlers (group Q12) and Tab.get/Browser.get (other PR).
- query_selector, query_selector_all and find_element_by_text, which are one-shot calls without a timeout.
- wait_for_ready_state, which was already bounded.
- CHANGELOG.md.

Heavy pages (reviewer item 2). I chose option (c): keep the hard bound at timeout + 0.5s and state the cost exactly. I did not add a larger or adaptive grace.

It records how long the event loop is blocked during one attempt with a large timeout:

| Nodes | Call | Total | Loop blocked (Python parsing) | Loop idle (waiting for Chrome) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20k | select | 0.65s | 0.38s | 0.27s |
| 50k | select | 2.27s | 1.66s | 0.6s |
| 50k | xpath | 2.06s | 1.34s | 0.72s |
| 100k | select | 6.36s | 3.54s | 2.82s |
| 100k | xpath | 4.00s | 3.28s | 0.71s |

"Tab.find, select, find_all, select_all, xpath, wait_for and tab(...), and the cloudflare helpers, now return or raise within about timeout + 0.5s when the browser never answers (for example while an alert() is open), instead of hanging. With timeout <= 0, find, select, find_all, select_all and wait_for still make one attempt without a bound, so they can still hang on a page blocked by a dialog. xpath bounds its attempt to 0.5s and returns []. An attempt that takes longer than timeout + 0.5s is now cut off. On pages with tens of thousands of nodes a single DOM query can take 2-6s, so calls with short timeouts there now time out or return [] where they used to return late."
